candidates.name: Ain Sokhna FSRU Gas Import Pipeline (Sonker berth to national grid)

values.PipelineName: Ain Sokhna FSRU Gas Import Pipeline
values.StartLocation: Sonker berth, Ain Sokhna Port (FSRU regasification berth)
values.EndLocation: National gas grid interconnection, Ain Sokhna
values.RouteNotes: Short onshore import connector (~17 km, 36-inch) laid by Petrojet/GASCO from the Sonker FSRU berth at Ain Sokhna to the national gas transmission grid; three new valve rooms. No official GIS located; endpoints from ministry inspection reporting.

candidates.researcher_notes: Match check: no existing Egypt gas row references Ain Sokhna, Sonker, SUMED, or an FSRU grid connector (57 rows in discovery_context.json reviewed) -> genuine miss, not matched_existing. Add-threshold met: (a) sponsor = GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, transmission operator) engineering/PM + Petrojet construction, EGAS state programme; (b) endpoints = Sonker FSRU berth, Ain Sokhna -> national gas grid, Suez governorate, Egypt; (c) concrete step = pipeline built 2024-2025, petroleum-minister site inspection May 2025, three valve rooms and 36-in/17-km line under active construction for the summer-2025 FSRU tie-in. Specs (36-inch dia, 17 km, three valve rooms) come from the May-2025 ministerial inspection reported by Daily News Egypt and Amwal Al Ghad -> SAME press event, so treated as one source, not two independent -> tier MEDIUM for the dimensional data. Existence and operating status are independently corroborated: Egypt Independent (2025-07-06) and Egypt Oil & Gas (Madbouly) both report the Sonker + SUMED FSRUs (Energos Power at Sonker, Energos Eskimo/Hoegh Galleon at SUMED) being connected to and feeding the national grid for peak-summer 2025; by July 2026 the three Ain Sokhna FSRUs are reported operating, hence Status=operating (was 'nearing grid connection' June 2025; construction is the conservative fallback if reviewer prefers). Borderline terminal-connector call: at 36-inch x 17 km with valve rooms and a distinct grid tie-in this is a substantial transmission connector worth a pipeline row (comparable to existing short Egyptian connectors like Idku-Abu Hummus / Damietta-SEGAS), so classed new_row rather than folded into the terminal entry. Entity caution: Owner=GASCO is the EGYPTIAN Natural Gas Company; entity_lookup returned only Norwegian 'Gassco' (ID 90) as a near match -- do NOT link this row to ID 90; GASCO Egypt is a separate entity (parent: Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company / EGAS). Owner is inferred from GASCO's builder/transmission-operator role (no source states legal ownership explicitly) -> low confidence on ownership specifically. Capacity, cost, and precise route/GIS unavailable; RouteAccuracy=approximate, no route staged (geometry -> routes repo). All 5 cited URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py. All sources English (source_language=en); no Arabic-only corroboration needed given English coverage. StartYear1 left blank: grid injection via this connector began peak-summer 2025 per the Status refs (Egypt Independent; Egypt Oil & Gas/Madbouly), but no source states a formal commissioning date for the pipeline itself — reviewer may set StartYear1=2025 from those same refs.

candidates.name: El Sadat–El Fayoum (Dahshour) Gas Pipeline

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints and corridor known from the GASCO EIA (Nov 2009): starts at the El Sadat off-take room, runs south ~76 km parallel to the SUMED crude line and the El Ameriya–Dashour gas pipeline, through 6th of October City (crossing Mehwar 26 July road, the 6th of October–El Wahat road, and the Cairo–El Faiyum road), terminating at Dahshour compression station. No GIS geometry located.

verifications.note: url_verifier.py FAILs the substring screen on this URL because it fetches raw PDF bytes as r.text (documented false-negative class in url_verifier.py's own docstring for PDF text extraction). Manually confirmed live (HTTP 200, 13.2MB real PDF) and content via `pdftotext` + direct page read: exact match to 'el sadat – el fayoum gas pipeline with 76 Km length and 32" diameter... starts from El Sadat off take room then extends toward south direction parallel to SUMID [SUMED] pipelines and El Ameriya Dashour pipeline for a distance about 76 km... until it reaches Dashour compression station (the end of the pipeline)', GASCO EIA, November 2009.

candidates.researcher_notes:
MATCH CHECK (rule 4, done first): re-checked against all 57 existing Egypt-gas rows in discovery_context.json AND the live GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260715.csv (filtered for Fayoum/Sadat/Faium/Dahshour/Dahshur across all columns — 6 hits, none a match). P3928 (Nubaria–Sadat, El Noubareya→El Sadat, 73 km/36 in) is the UPSTREAM feeder into El Sadat — different corridor, different endpoints. P3930 (New Administrative Capital–Dahshur, 70 km/32 in) reaches Dahshour from New Administrative Capital, a different origin altogether. P6686 (New Fayoum Gas Pipeline, construction, 40 km, 16/24 in) is a lateral into New Fayoum City (a newer satellite-city gas connection), not the historic El Sadat→El Fayoum trunk. P0477/P6697–P6702 (South Valley Gas Pipeline family) start AT Dahshour and run south to Aswan — downstream of, not overlapping with, this segment. None of the 57 rows covers El Sadat→Dahshour/El Fayoum itself. => new_row, not matched_existing.

ADD-THRESHOLD (all three legs met): (a) sponsor = EGAS (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co.) / GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Co., the promoter named on both cited documents); (b) endpoints = Egypt, El Sadat off-take room → Dahshour compression station (Nile Delta→Giza/6th-of-October corridor feeding Upper Egypt + Cairo); (c) concrete step = EIB loan SIGNED 09/10/2008 for the EGAS Gas Grid Reinforcement program (five pipelines, ~835 km total, EUR 280M EIB / EUR 588M total cost) plus a completed, dated Environmental Impact Assessment (GASCO, Nov 2009) with final engineered route and specs — well past MOU/rumor stage.

SOURCES (2 independent, both verified live + content-confirmed):
1. GASCO EIA PDF (eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia14_en.pdf, Nov 2009) — PRIMARY project document, author = promoter (GASCO). States verbatim: 76 km, 32-inch, El Sadat off-take room → south, parallel to SUMED + El Ameriya-Dashour lines, through 6th of October City, terminating at Dahshour compression station. This is the same document also mirrored at yumpu.com (the consolidator's second evidence URL) — NOT counted as a second independent source since it's one underlying document; cited the eib.org original instead since yumpu's page-flip viewer doesn't serve extractable text to automated tools (confirmed via pdftotext against the downloaded PDF).
2. EIB project page (eib.org/en/projects/all/20070088) — author = lender (EIB), independent of the promoter. Confirms 'Elsadat-Elfayoum' as one of five named EIA/segments within the same financed program, loan signed 2008, promoter EGAS/GASCO, total program cost.
These two are independently authored (promoter vs. lender) but both trace to the same 2007–2009 EIB financing event, so I'm rating EXISTENCE/NAME as corroborated by 2 sources but the exact LENGTH/DIAMETER numbers as effectively single-primary-sourced — hence tier=medium, not high.

NON-CITABLE THIRD SOURCE (informs confidence, NOT used as a ref — wikidot is blocklisted per standing rule 1 / url_verifier.py BLOCKLIST_HOSTS): ENPPI's own project-reference portfolio lists 'El Nubaria/El Sadat & El Sadat/El Fayoum Pipelines,' client GASCO, EPC timeframe 2010/2012, but gives DIFFERENT specs for the El Sadat/El Fayoum leg: 42-inch, 80 km (vs. the 2009 EIA's 32-inch/76 km). This is a real, independently-tracked EPC project confirming the segment exists and was built ~2010–2012, but the spec discrepancy (32 in/76 km design-stage vs. 42 in/80 km as-built per the EPC contractor) is flagged for reviewer attention — staged LengthKnown/Diameter reflect the primary EIA design values, not the possibly-revised as-built ENPPI figures, since ENPPI can't be cited to override them.

STATUS: set to 'operating' by inference, not direct citation — flag before applying. Both citable sources are pre-construction (financing signed 2008, EIA Nov 2009); I found no citable EN source directly confirming commissioning/completion. The inference rests on: (a) the non-citable ENPPI reference showing EPC execution 2010–2012; (b) both bracketing segments in the same EGAS Gas Grid Reinforcement corridor — upstream P3928 (Nubaria–Sadat) and downstream P0477/P6697–P6702 (Dahshour–Aswan South Valley family) — are long-since 'operating' in the live GEM sheet, and this segment is the missing middle link needed to complete that corridor; (c) 17 years have passed since financing/EIA. Recommend a targeted GASCO/EGAS annual-report or current satellite-imagery check to convert this from inferred to directly-sourced before the row goes live.

OWNER: set to 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co [100.%]' (entity_lookup.py confirmed exact existing-entity match, no duplicate) to match the sibling-row convention on P3928/P3930/P0477 (all EGAS-owned per the live sheet), consistent with the project's own EGAS/GASCO promoter identification. Per project convention (owner refs live on the separate ProjectID-keyed operators/owners tab, not this tracker's ref columns), no inline 'Owner [ref]' is staged here.

NOT POPULATED (left blank rather than guessed, per no-fabrication rule): StartState/Province, EndState/Province (El Sadat sits in Menoufia/Beheira border country, Dahshour in Giza Governorate, but I did not find a citable source pinning the precise administrative province for either endpoint of THIS pipeline specifically); ConstructionYear/StartYear1 (no citable specific year — only the non-citable ENPPI 2010/2012 EPC window); ProjectLevelCost (EIB's EUR 588M total is for the WHOLE five-pipeline, 835 km reinforcement program, not attributable to this one 76 km segment without fabricating an allocation); FIDStatus (only populated when Status=proposed, per controlled_vocab.md).

CONFIDENCE = medium overall: existence/identity/route corroborated by 2 independently-authored, verified, citable sources (GASCO EIA + EIB project page) plus a non-citable third (ENPPI); exact length/diameter numbers effectively single-primary-sourced (the EIA) with a conflicting as-built figure from the non-citable ENPPI reference; operating status is inferred from strong circumstantial/corridor evidence, not directly cited — surface this caveat prominently before staging to the live sheet.

candidates.name: Gaza Marine–El Arish Offshore Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Threshold leg (c) fails at the pipeline level. Legs (a) sponsor [EGAS 45% operator, PIF 27.5%, CCC 27.5%] and (b) endpoints [Gaza Marine field -> El Arish, Egypt] are met, but there is no concrete step specific to THIS pipeline. The MoU (Feb 2021), Framework Agreement (Oct 2022) and Israeli preliminary approval (June 2023) all pertain to the upstream Gaza Marine FIELD development consortium, not to a committed pipeline (no pipeline FEED/EPC award, permit, tender, or FID). The El Arish subsea route is only one competing commercialization option (vs Israel's Ashdod), and the whole scheme has been dormant since Oct 2023 with no infrastructure work; as of Aug 2025 nothing has commenced. Pipeline is a routing concept tied to a stalled, never-developed field -> monitor.
candidates.researcher_notes: NOT matched_existing: distinct from P3657 (Israel-Egypt Offshore, an Israel->Egypt Leviathan/Tamar export concept, 6.7 bcm, different origin/sponsor) and from P5276 (Israel->Gaza supply, opposite direction; not in the Egypt roster). Gaza Marine is a separate ~28-30 bcm field in Palestinian waters, ~35 km offshore Gaza, discovered 2000. The Egyptian development option: ~50-60 km (~40-mile) subsea line delivering Gaza Marine gas to the Egyptian grid at El Arish for processing, with in-system swap for Idku LNG export. Confidence tier MEDIUM: two independent sources agree on the core facts (MESP long-form 2024-02; Middle East Eye 2022-10), corroborated by MEES, Egypt Oil & Gas, and Wikipedia 'Natural gas in the Gaza Strip' — but they are largely secondary/analytical and there is no primary pipeline milestone (no route, no FEED/EPC, no tender). Ownership stakes (EGAS 45% / PIF 27.5% / CCC 27.5%) and Cheiron as EGAS technical lead are consistently reported. Route: no defined corridor; would be an offshore Gaza->Sinai coast line, but nothing GIS-grade exists. Recommend MONITOR for a pipeline-specific milestone (route defined, FEED/EPC award, or tender) before creating a GEM row; revisit if Gaza-war ceasefire revives field development.

candidates.name: Libya–Egypt Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (b) country+region/endpoints (and arguably leg a, dedicated sponsor). No Egypt–Libya gas interconnector concept has fixed endpoints, route, or capacity. The Jan 2026 Petrojet–NOC MoU is a broad oil/gas/mining cooperation framework that only 'explores the feasibility of transporting crude oil and natural gas between the two countries' — a study-level intent, not a pipeline project with a sponsor, defined corridor, or physical scope.
candidates.researcher_notes: Re-checked match-to-existing against all 57 Egypt gas rows in discovery_context.json: no Libya–Egypt (or Salloum/Tobruk/Libya-border) gas interconnector exists in GGIT — confirmed genuine absence, not a matched row. CONFIRMED the Jan 25 2026 Petrojet–NOC MoU signed at the Libya Energy & Economic Summit in Tripoli (signatories Waleed Lotfy, PETROJET chairman; Masoud Suleman, NOC chairman) via two independent English sources: egyptoil-gas.com and logupdateafrica.com (both verified 200 + content; Egypt State Information Service sis.gov.eg corroborates in search results but its URL failed url_verifier on SSLError, not cited). All independent accounts agree the MoU spans oil, gas AND mining and only commits to STUDYING feasibility of moving crude and gas between the countries — no gas-pipeline sponsor, no route, no endpoints, no capacity, no length. This is a recurring cross-border project family with a long non-delivery record: 1997 Tobruk–Sidi Krir crude plan and 2000 ~$100m Altube JV (crude to Egypt / Egyptian gas to Libya) never built (egyptoil-gas 2019 feature, verified); Nov 2022 NOC chairman Bengdara at ADIPEC floated a Libya→Damietta gas export line alongside a Greece line and Greenstream (pipeline-journal, verified) — a Libya-export study, distinct from and not carried forward into the 2026 MoU. Confidence tier medium: the 2026 MoU itself is well-corroborated (2+ independent), but the underlying pipeline remains pre-feasibility with no physical scope. Recommend MONITOR — revisit if a dedicated gas-interconnector feasibility study, FEED, defined route/endpoints, or capacity is announced.

Specs (127 km, 24 in, 7 MMcf/d, EGP 336 million, 2006) are stated by Oil & Gas Journal (Sept 2007), attributing the work to Gasco — verified via url_verifier (200 + 'Shukeir' present), confirmed verbatim: 'Also during 2006, Gasco completed the Shukeir-Hurgada pipeline, 127 km (79 miles) of 24 in. that can handle 7 MMcfd of gas for the Red Sea Governorate ... GulfPub's own gas layer also carries a small 'Zeit Bay - Ras Shukheir Line' tie-in (2 km, 16 in) explicitly described as feeding into 'the Ras Shukheir - Hurghada Pipeline' — further reinforcing this is a real, named trunk in an independently-maintained industry database, not an artifact of one journalist's reporting. candidates.name: Taba–Sharm El-Sheikh Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Fails the corroboration leg (existence of an already-built line needs >=2 independent sources; a single OGJ story tracing to GASCO is one source), not the sponsor/endpoints/concrete-step legs.
candidates.researcher_notes:
SUPERSEDES a prior 2026-07-09 shard on this same slug that had classed this new_row at tier=medium — I re-read that shard's two 'corroborating' sources myself and they do not hold up, so I am overriding to monitor rather than defending the earlier call.

MATCH-TO-EXISTING RE-CHECKED, NO MATCH: confirmed against discovery_context.json (57 existing Egypt-gas rows) that no GEM row runs south down the Sinai east coast. P0436 (Arab Gas Pipeline segment, Arish–Taba) and P7482 (AGP Taba–Aqaba subsea) both sit at the Taba node but point away from this route (north/east toward the AGP export corridor), matching the queue note. So this would be a genuine gap, not a rename — but it does not clear the corroboration bar below.

ONLY REAL SOURCE: OGJ (Sep 2007 trade journal, verified via url_verifier.py — 200 + 'Taba' present) describing GASCO building a 220 km, 20-inch, ~6 MMcfd line Taba–Nuweiba–Dahab–Sharm El-Sheikh, online early 2007 at ~L.E. 511M, serving en-route towns/hotels and power stations. This traces entirely to GASCO as the named source.

PRIOR SHARD'S 'CORROBORATION' DOES NOT HOLD UP ON RE-READ: (1) the EDEPCO government page on the Sharm El-Sheikh power plant does confirm the plant is natural-gas/diesel-fired ('غاز طبيعي / سولار'), but says nothing about how gas reaches the plant (pipeline vs. trucked LNG/CNG, both common for isolated Egyptian coastal plants) and gives no date — it does not confirm this specific 2007 pipeline. (2) The Youm7 article is not from 2021 background context but is itself a Nov-2021 announcement of newly completed CNG *vehicle* fueling stations in Sharm El-Sheikh, explicitly framed as implementing 'presidential directives to transform Sharm El-Sheikh into a sustainable green city' ahead of COP27 — i.e., NEW infrastructure in 2021, not evidence of a mature trunk operating since 2007. Neither source actually confirms the pipeline's route, length, diameter, or in-service date; the earlier shard's inference ('a gas-fired plant + CNG stations can't exist without a transmission trunk from Taba') is a plausibility argument, not independent confirmation, and it doesn't rule out trucked/LNG supply.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE FOUND (does not conclusively disprove existence, but undercuts a mature-since-2007 trunk feeding hotels): Egypt Oil & Gas (2016-08-23) covers a new natural-gas plant for Sharm El-Sheikh's Al Salam City described as 'the first of its kind in Sharm El Sheikh area'; Egypt Oil & Gas (2020-04-26) covers a still-in-progress ('90% complete', EGP 250M) Sinai Gas project delivering gas to Nabaq Bay in Sharm; Egypt Oil & Gas (2020-12-27) covers Sharm El-Sheikh's first-ever CNG vehicle station; and 2022 COP27-era coverage frames citywide tourist-facility gas conversion in Sharm as a new, first-of-kind push toward a 'green city'. This 2016–2022 drumbeat of 'first ever' gas-infrastructure milestones in Sharm El-Sheikh sits awkwardly next to a claim that a 220 km/6 MMcfd trunk has already been serving its hotels and tourist villages since early 2007 — plausible reconciliations exist (a 2007 trunk feeding only the power stations, with hotel/vehicle last-mile buildout arriving in phases through the 2020s) but none was found and verified.

ALSO NOTE: OGJ's '6 MMcfd' capacity figure looks too small for a line also billed as serving four power stations, which is either a units/typo error in the sole source or a sign the 2007 line was minor (towns/hotels only) — another reason not to stage numbers off this single source.

SOURCE CHECKED AND REJECTED: the EIB/PETROSAFE 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' EIA (eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia4_en.pdf, Nov 2007) is a DIFFERENT project — a 36-inch North Sinai loop, El-Tena East→El-Areish — not this South Sinai coastal 20-inch line; does not corroborate.

SEARCHED, NOT FOUND: any GASCO/EGAS network GIS map or annual report with route-level Sinai detail (gasco.com.eg's own Gas Grid page only says generically 'extending east to Sinai... along the coast of the Red Sea'); no contemporaneous Arabic-language press (2006–2008) on this specific project despite targeted search.

RECOMMEND: keep on watchlist. A future pass should try a GASCO/EGAS GIS asset map, an Arabic retrospective explicitly naming this route, or company financial/annual-report disclosure — any of which, if found, would supply the missing second source. Not new_row absent that; not matched_existing since no GEM row covers this corridor.
